rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The repeated conditional leaves its answer unstated, intensifying the warning that God could hasten worldly destruction for those spreading the slander and join it to the afterlife's punishment.
rows.anchor: فلولا فضل الله عليكم ورحمته بكم لعجل هلاك المحبين لشيوع ذلك بعذاب الدنيا ليكون موصولا بعذاب الآخرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's gentleness removes ignorance through messengers, revealed books, and legal limits that deter wrongdoing and lead to taqwa, knowledge's fruit.
rows.anchor: في نصب ما يزيل جهلكم بما يحفظ من سرائركم بإرسال الرسل وإنزال الكتب ونصب الحدود

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Raʾfa is the gentlest and most complete mercy: it preserves the recipient along the soundest path so that what merits pardon can emerge.
rows.anchor: فإن الرأفة كما تقدم في الحج وغيرها تقيم المرؤوف به لأنها ألطف الرحمة وأبلغها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's preserving care may operate by establishing proofs, or additionally by creating guidance in the heart of a receptive person who submits readily.
rows.anchor: إلى ذلك الفعل بخلق الهداية في القلب بما للمرؤوف به من الوصلة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God is merciful by raising the recipients' ranks through the approved deeds that grow from this preserving care.
rows.anchor: بما يثبت لكم من الدرجات على ما منحكم به من ثمرات ذلك الحفظ من الأعمال المرضية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The omitted answer is that without God's favor and mercy people would wander blindly in ignorance, fall into strife and destruction, and reach lasting punishment.
rows.anchor: فثارت بينكم الفتن حتى تفانيكم ووصلتم إلى العذاب الدائم بعد الهم اللازم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The believers are urged to make every effort not to imitate Satan or follow any path he beautifies; the verb form also hints at pardon for inadvertent slips.
rows.anchor: لا تقتدوا به ولا تسلكوا مسالكه التي يحمل على سلوكها بتزيينها في شيء من الأشياء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The repeated explicit phrase, instead of a pronoun, heightens aversion; following Satan is framed as deliberate resolve rather than mistake or forgetfulness.
rows.anchor: بعزم ثابت من غير أن يكون مخطئا أو ناسيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Satan commands extreme ugliness and whatever the law does not permit; he aims first at the greatest deviation and descends to lesser evil if thwarted.
rows.anchor: فإن لم يصل تنزل إلى أدناه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One who follows Satan takes on his deeds and sinks to utter baseness; spelling out Satan again makes the warning stronger than a pronoun would.
rows.anchor: عمل بعمله , فصار في غاية السفول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's favor purifies souls and lifts them above base desires, while His mercy grants repentance that expiates the deficient speech and low actions ignorance caused.
rows.anchor: بإكرامكم ورفعتكم بشرع التوبة المكفرة لما جر إليه الجهل

words: ما زكى منكم من أحد أبدا
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Zakkā means to purify and cause to grow; the repeated min emphasizes that not one person is excluded, and abadan extends the denial across all time.
rows.anchor: وأكد الاستغراق بقوله : { من أحد }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God alone purifies whom He wills from the soul's impurities and heart's diseases: He protected some from the slander and left others to fail.
rows.anchor: جميع أدناس نفسه وأمراض قلبه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God hears every utterance and knows thoughts, states, and deeds, so He knows who is fit for purification; believers should thank Him and patiently continue kindness toward others.
rows.anchor: بكل ما يخطر في بالهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yaʾtal means to swear an emphatic oath; the context makes an explicit negative particle unnecessary before the command not to withhold help.
rows.anchor: أي يحلف مبالغا في اليمين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The people of virtue are those God has equipped with knowledge and good character to benefit others; the people of means are those granted worldly abundance.
rows.anchor: الذين جعلتهم بما آتيتهم من العلم والأخلاق الصالحة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kin, the poor even without kinship, and emigrants who left family, homes, and wealth for God's path are each grounds for generosity; the three qualities may describe one person, as in Mistah's case.
rows.anchor: الذين لا يجدون ما يغنيهم وإن لم تكن لهم قرابة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling these qualities reasons to pardon shows that even the purified among non-infallible people may stumble, then repentance restores them; conjunction emphasizes each trait when one person has all three.
rows.anchor: دليل على أن الزاكي من غير المعصومين قد يزل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ʿAfw is to erase the offender's slip and cover it with forbearance until no trace remains.
rows.anchor: عن زللهم بأن يمحوه ويغطوه بما يسلبونه عليه من أستار الحلم حتى لا يبقى له أثر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Safh is to turn away altogether and not bring the offense to mind; al-ṣafūḥ also means generous.
rows.anchor: فلا يخطروه لهم على بال

words: ألا تحبون أن يغفر الله لكم
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The gracious appeal urges the virtuous to treat others as they wish God to treat them, while warning that harshness toward others invites strict treatment in return.
rows.anchor: مرغبا في أن يفعلوا بغيرهم ما يحبون أن يفعل بهم

words: ألا تحبون أن يغفر الله لكم
rows.speaker: عائشة
rows.claim: A report from ʿĀʾisha, which the author calls sound, says Abū Bakr swore after God cleared ʿĀʾisha of slander that he would stop supporting his cousin Mistah, who had joined the slanderers.
rows.anchor: أن أباها رضي الله تعالى عنه كان حلف

words: ألا تحبون أن يغفر الله لكم
rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Al-Aṣbahānī's tafsir reports from Ibn ʿAbbās that some Companions, including Abū Bakr, swore not to give alms or aid to a man who had spoken about the slander.
rows.anchor: وفي تفسير الأصبهاني عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's naming Abū Bakr one of the people of virtue is an exceptional honor, and he fulfilled the command by forgiving the slanderer and continuing his support.
rows.anchor: للصديق بأنه من أولي الفضل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God may erase believers' sins and then favor them with mercy as they have shown mercy to others; recompense matches the deed.
rows.anchor: فإن الجزاء من جنس العمل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The plural houses means the walls of houses and indicates that the niche is a general kind, not a single one; the singularity of its light fittings signals its great rarity.
rows.anchor: دلالة على أن المراد بالمشكاة الجنس لا الواحد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's permission means He enables, permits, recommends, or makes obligatory; raising the houses is physical in construction and spiritual through sincere good works.
rows.anchor: حسا في البناء , ومعنى بإخلاصها للعمل الصالح

rows.speaker: عبد الله بن عمرو
rows.claim: Abū Dāwūd reports from ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAmr that the Prophet sought refuge in God when entering a mosque; ʿUqba ibn Muslim adds that Satan then says the person is protected for the day. The author gives no grading.
rows.anchor: عن عبد الله بن عمرو رضي الله عنهما عن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's name is remembered there by any person He permits, in remembrance free of admixture or deceit.
rows.anchor: أي ذكرا صافيا عن شوب , وخالصا عن غش

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yusabbiḥu here means both praying and declaring God transcendent, and the worship is for Him alone.
rows.anchor: فيها بالغدو } أي الإبكار , بصلاة الصبح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Dawn denotes the morning prayer and evenings denote the remaining prayers; beginning and ending their work with remembrance preserves and blesses the intervening activity.
rows.anchor: ويختمونها بذكره ليحفظوا فيما بين ذلك ويبارك لهم

rows.speaker: البغوي
rows.claim: Al-Baghawī says the plural al-āṣāl includes ẓuhr, ʿaṣr, maghrib, and ʿishāʾ.
rows.anchor: قال البغوي : لأن اسم الأصيل يجمعها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Trade includes sales or other profitable dealings; sale is separately mentioned because people may sell possessions to meet necessities, and al-bayʿ can mean either acquiring by purchase or disposing by sale.
rows.anchor: والبيع يطلق بالاشتراك على التحصيل الذي هو الشرى

words: لا تلهيهم تجارة ولا بيع عن ذكر الله
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Neither kind of business distracts these men from God's remembrance, through prayer or otherwise; they remain in continual awareness and watchfulness of Him.
rows.anchor: فهم كل وقت في شهود ومراقبة لمن تعرف إليهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Prayer is named explicitly after remembrance to stress guarding its time and all its requirements, even the least adequate performance; the wording does not demand the highest degree of perfection.
rows.anchor: أعادها بعد ذكرها بالتسبيح تصريحا بها تأكيدا لها وحثا على حفظ وقتها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Zakat is the purification and growth of bodies, complementing prayer's purification of spirits.
rows.anchor: التي هي زكاة الأشباح ونماؤها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although women's attendance at mosques is an established sunnah, specifying men here signals that women's prayer at home is better; the supporting reports follow in the next segment.
rows.anchor: مع أن حضور النساء المساجد سنة شهيرة

rows.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود
rows.claim: Abū Dāwūd and Ibn Khuzayma report from Ibn Masʿūd that a woman's prayer in the more private part of her home is better; the source glosses al-mikhdaʿ as a storage closet. No grading is stated.
rows.anchor: صلاة المرأة في بيتها أفضل من صلاتها في حجرتها

rows.speaker: أم سلمة
rows.claim: A report from Umm Salama, cited from Aḥmad, al-Ṭabarānī, Ibn Khuzayma, and al-Ḥākim, says the best mosque for women is the innermost part of their homes. No grading is stated.
rows.anchor: خير مساجد النساء قعر بيوتهن

rows.speaker: أم حميدة
rows.claim: Umm Ḥumayd asked to pray with the Prophet; he said prayer at home was better, increasingly so from private room to house to local mosque to his mosque. She built a mosque in the darkest, farthest part of her home and prayed there until death.
rows.anchor: عن أم حميدة امرأة أبي حميد الساعدي رضي الله عنهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The feared day is the Resurrection, when the hearts and eyes turn between hope of salvation and fear of destruction because of its terror.
rows.anchor: وهو يوم القيامة , هو بحيث { تتقلب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The two written tāʾs in tatqallabu emphasize the visible intensity of the hearts' and eyes' turning.
rows.anchor: بما أشار إليه إثبات التاءين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: As an inward reading of the light parable, the mosques are niches, men are glass, hearts are lamps, their prompting meanings are radiance, purified upright bodies are the tree, and their beautiful secrets are its oil.
rows.anchor: المصابيح هي القلوب , وتلألؤها ما تشتمل عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author mentions a report that mosques are to heaven's people what stars are to earth's people, without giving its authority or a grading.
rows.anchor: وقد ورد في بعض الأخبار أن المساجد لأهل السماوات كالنجوم لأهل الأرض

rows.speaker: ابن عمر
rows.claim: Al-Ṭabarānī's al-Awsaṭ reports from Ibn ʿUmar an inward gloss: the niche is Muḥammad's interior, the glass his heart, the lamp its light, Abraham the tree, and neither east nor west means neither Jew nor Christian. No grading is given.
rows.anchor: وفي معجم الطبراني في الأوسط عن ابن عمر رضي الله عنهما : ( كمسكاة ) قال : جوف محمد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They do these acts so God may reward their best deeds and forgive the bad, then increase their reward by grace beyond what justice alone requires.
rows.anchor: أي يفعلون ذلك ليجزيهم { الله }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author adduces prophetic signs: trees came bowing when summoned and returned when told, animals obeyed, a trembling mountain yielded, palms and stones gathered and returned on command, water sprang from earth, and a well overflowed when struck by an arrow.
rows.anchor: الضب وغيره من الحيوانات العجم فأطاعته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Even an infant summoned by the Prophet testified to him, which the author explains by the child's still-original fitra; these signs support the verse's apparent sense and honor the Prophet without conflict or contradiction of scripture.
rows.anchor: دال على ظاعر الآية المقتضي لزيادة شرفه

rows.speaker: أبو جعفر بن الزبير
rows.claim: Abū Jaʿfar ibn al-Zubayr says al-Nūr's rulings and disclosures distinguish good from evil: exposure of the ifk and hypocrites, the promise to the rightly guided caliphs, and the Khandaq hypocrites' exposure together form a furqān that strengthens faith and proves the Messenger.
rows.anchor: أبو جعفر بن الزبير في برهانه : لما تضمنت سورة النور

rows.speaker: أبو جعفر بن الزبير
rows.claim: Ibn al-Zubayr says this context clarifies the Messenger's high standing in 24:63 and is appropriately followed by the opening declaration of the Furqān.
rows.anchor: ويوضح مضمن قوله 77 ( { ا تجعلوا دعاء الرسول بينكم } ) 77

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After mentioning the revealer, the Furqān, and its recipient generally, the passage now details them in that order, beginning with God as sole sovereign and the universal scope of His message.
rows.anchor: ذكر الفرقان والمنزل عليه على طريق الإجمال , أتبع ذلك تفصيله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because God alone owns the heavens and earth, there is no reason to deny that He sends a messenger to everyone within them.
rows.anchor: فلا إنكار لأن يرسل رسولا إلى كل من فيهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God has no child who could act arrogantly toward His messenger.
rows.anchor: ولم يتخذ ولدا } ليتكبر على رسوله

words: ولم يكن له شريك في الملك
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: No partner can oppose or share God's messengership, leaving some creation outside His message or subject to another's command.
rows.anchor: في الملك } ليناقضه في الرسالة أو يقاسمه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A thing's inability to cross its created limit or change its kind demonstrates that it is created and governed; creatures cannot fully explain this constraint.
rows.anchor: دالا على أنه مخلوق مربوب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Khalaqa means bringing something into existence with due measure and proportion.
rows.anchor: أحدث إحداثا مراعي فيه التقدير والتسوية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Everything includes alleged divine offspring, partners, and all else; God fitted each thing without disparity for its proper purpose and enabled it for that end.
rows.anchor: أي مما ادعى فيه الولدية أو الشرك وغيره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After the proof that God alone is deity, the author marvels at idolaters for taking other gods and signals contempt by leaving the agent implicit.
rows.anchor: عجب منهم لكل ذي عقل في جملة حالية فيما خالفوا ما لهم من المشاهدة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Idols cannot create anything and are themselves created, as shown by their change and subjection to God's will and by their worshippers carving or shaping them.
rows.anchor: أي لا أعجز منهم , لا يكون منهم إيجاد شيء

words: ولا يملكون لأنفسهم ضرا ولا نفعا
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Idols cannot avert harm or secure benefit even for themselves; the indefinite harm is comprehensive, and even retaining an unchanged state is beyond them.
rows.anchor: ولذلك قدمه , ونكره ليعم

words: ولا يملكون لأنفسهم ضرا ولا نفعا
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Worshippers may acquire some benefit only by God's will and are therefore superior to idols; the worship of a superior by an inferior is irrational.
rows.anchor: فهم أعلى منهم وعبادة الأعلى لمن دونه ليست من أفعال العقلاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse repeats the verb for owning, places death before more common life, then adds resurrection; each inability independently disproves the idols' divinity despite the causal sequence.
rows.anchor: قدم الموت لأن الحياة أكثر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet's distant-form address voices intense complaint and sorrow at his people's abandonment of the Qurʾān, despite their reasons to draw near to it.
rows.anchor: شدة التحرق , وعظيم التحزن كما يشير إليه إثبات يا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The criminals' hostility toward the Prophet arises from envy; God made such enemies for earlier prophets too, raising their rank, and they should be patient as their predecessors were.
rows.anchor: حسدا لك , وعطف عليه : { وكذلك }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God has marked these criminals by eagerness to sever bonds that should connect people and has led them astray as a humiliation; He will guide some through the Prophet and support him over others.
rows.anchor: على الشغف بقطع ما يقتضي الوصل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet need not grieve: God will raise allies from among the guided, aid them over enemies as He aided earlier prophets, and honor his people by sparing them annihilation for his sake.
rows.anchor: لا تحزن فلنجعلن لك وليا ممن نهديه للإيمان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God suffices as guide for those decreed blessed and as helper against those decreed wretched, answering the apparent improbability created by the many enemies.
rows.anchor: { هاديا } يهدي بك من قضى بسعادته { ونصيرا * } ينصرك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The disbelievers' objection follows the complaint that they abandoned the Qurʾān and the assurance of God's aid; the explicit label 'those who disbelieved' highlights the trait behind their speech.
rows.anchor: ولما ذكر سبحانه شكايته من هجرانهم للقرآن , وقرر

words: لولا نزل عليه القرآن جملة واحدة
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The disbelievers hide envy and hostility behind their demand for one-time revelation, although their reason recognizes the Qurʾān as God's inimitable speech whether revealed in parts or all at once.
rows.anchor: القرآن كلام لإعجازه لهم متفرقا , فضلا عن كونه مجتمعا

words: لولا نزل عليه القرآن جملة واحدة
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They also conceal the clear effects of the Qurʾān that testify to God's oneness and other divine attributes.
rows.anchor: وغطوا ما وضح لهم من آثاره الظاهرة الشاهد بوحدانيته
